Name: Anonymity
Context: Graduates submit career-office questionnaires, and respondents should not be identifiable to third parties.
Problems: Responses could be associated with an identifiable graduate.
Forces: Maintaining an adequately large anonymity set is necessary.
Benefits: Allows participation without directly revealing the respondent identity.
Limits the ability to link questionnaire submissions to individual graduates.
Liabilities: Anonymity may reduce accountability and complicate abuse investigation.
Some implementations incur performance and usability costs.
Protection depends on the size and properties of the anonymity set.
